html:
Hyderabad State, the Nizam's Dominions, was the largest princely state in India, ruled by the Nizams in the Deccan from 1724 to 1948.

Its founder, Asaf Jah I, was a Mughal governor who made himself independent as the Mughal Empire weakened. His successors held the old lands of Golconda and the Deccan, and moved the capital to Hyderabad in 1763. They fought the Marathas and Tipu Sultan and leaned on the British.

On the 1800 map the Nizam had just signed a subsidiary alliance with the East India Company in 1798. He paid for British troops in his state, and in 1800 gave up lands to cover the cost. Later Nizams kept great wealth: Mir Osman Ali Khan was called the richest man in the world. In 1948 the Nizam refused to join India, and the Indian army took the state in Operation Polo. See also Berar.
sum: Hyderabad State, the Nizam's Dominions, was the largest princely state in India, ruled by the Nizams in the Deccan from 1724 to 1948.
